title: The launch review
fullTitle: The Launch Review Your Demo Never Shows

scenes.narration: The demo went perfectly. Every screen loaded. So why start a launch review with questions the demo cannot answer?
captions: The demo went perfectly. Every screen loaded.
So why start a launch review with questions the demo cannot answer?

scenes.narration: A demo shows one person doing everything right. It never shows a customer asking for someone else's data, a payment retried after a lost response, or a dashboard labelled live.
captions: A demo shows one person doing everything right.
It never shows someone else's data, a retried payment, or a stale "Live".

scenes.narration: Web Reality Checks turns each question into a short film. Reproduce the flaw. Prove the test can fail. Apply the smallest repair. Run the same test again.
captions: Each question becomes a short film.

scenes.narration: Pay once, lose the response, retry: two attempts, two orders. After the repair: two attempts, one order. Real numbers from the fixture.
captions: Pay once, lose the response, retry: 2 attempts, 2 orders.

scenes.narration: Another fixture shows a Live label over a ten-minute-old reading. The label described the page, not the measurement.
captions: A Live label over a ten-minute-old reading.
The label described the page, not the measurement.

scenes.narration: Five arcs, from trust and access to experience and speed, become ten questions you can put to any team or vendor.
captions: Five arcs become ten questions for any team or vendor.

scenes.narration: Not an audit, not a certification. The fixtures are synthetic, and every episode states what it does not prove.
captions: Not an audit. Not a certification.
Synthetic fixtures. Every episode states its limits.

scenes.narration: Clone the fixtures, run the tests, and take the questions to your next launch meeting. The repository, linked below.
captions: Clone the fixtures. Run the tests.
